details: Bitcoin's price surged by 2.4% to $84,489.25, benefiting from a broader rebound in technology stocks. Simultaneously, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) moved forward with finalized stablecoin rules, a development expected to positively impact programmable cryptocurrencies like Ethereum and Solana. Additionally, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs registered significant inflows, totaling $527 million.
title: Bitcoin Rises, OCC Finalizes Stablecoin Rules Amid Tech Rally

details: XRP experienced a substantial increase in its market capitalization, rising by approximately $4.1 billion within a 24-hour period to reach around $85.7 billion. This surge is primarily attributed to a broader rebound across the cryptocurrency market, coupled with an active derivatives market and a short squeeze that propelled its price upwards.
title: XRP Market Cap Jumps $4.1 Billion in 24 Hours

details: Bitcoin's 28-day volatility has reached near its 2026 lows, with the cryptocurrency trading within a tight range of $80,000 to $84,000. Traders are reportedly bracing for upcoming macroeconomic events, including the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on October 28 and the U.S. midterm elections on November 3. Despite the low volatility, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows of 6,436 BTC on October 19.
title: Bitcoin Volatility Nears Lows Before Fed Decision, US Midterms

details: LCX is set to initiate a community vote on October 22nd to determine which blockchain network will be integrated next into its Liberty DEX. The blockchain that garners the most votes from the community will proceed with integration.
title: LCX to Hold Community Vote for Next Liberty DEX Blockchain

details: The NEXO token is scheduled for a listing on the Kraken cryptocurrency exchange, with trading expected to commence on October 22nd. This listing aims to enhance the token's accessibility and liquidity for a wider range of investors.
title: NEXO Token to Be Listed on Kraken Exchange October 22nd

details: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's (OCC) recently finalized stablecoin rules have ignited a debate between traditional banking institutions and the cryptocurrency industry. The core of the dispute revolves around the treatment of third-party yield. The Blockchain Association argues that the regulation misinterprets statutory language, raising questions about the competitive landscape between stablecoins and traditional deposit products.
title: OCC Stablecoin Rules Spark Debate Over Third-Party Yield

details: Jurrien Timmer, Fidelity's Director of Global Macro, has suggested that any potential "AI bubble" is more likely to be found in debt markets rather than stock valuations. He pointed to CoreWeave bond yields surpassing 15% as an indicator, implying that credit investors are approaching the AI buildout with caution. This broader economic sentiment could indirectly influence investor confidence in the crypto market.
title: Fidelity: AI Bubble Risk in Debt Markets, Not Stock Valuations
